displayName: Smart PR Review — GitHub & Azure DevOps PR Review with AI
description: Review GitHub and Azure DevOps pull requests inside VS Code: diffs, comments, suggestions and votes.
config.azureDevOpsHosts: Azure DevOps Server hosts (for example `tfs.contoso.com`). Only hosts listed here receive your Azure DevOps credentials.
viewContainer.title: Smart PR Review
welcome.signedOut:
Sign in to GitHub to review the pull requests of this repository.
[Sign In to GitHub](command:smartPrReview.signIn)
welcome.noRepository: Open a folder that contains a Git repository whose remote is on GitHub or Azure DevOps. Git must be installed.
welcome.unsupported: This repository's remote is not on GitHub or Azure DevOps. For Azure DevOps Server, add its host to the setting `smartPrReview.azureDevOps.hosts` and reload the window.
welcome.signedOutAzureDevOps:
Sign in to Azure DevOps to review the pull requests of this repository.
[Sign In with Microsoft](command:smartPrReview.signIn)
[Use a Personal Access Token](command:smartPrReview.setAzureDevOpsPat)
welcome.signedOutAzureDevOpsServer:
Azure DevOps Server needs a Personal Access Token with the Code (Read & Write) scope.
[Enter Personal Access Token](command:smartPrReview.setAzureDevOpsPat)
command.setAzureDevOpsPat: Set Azure DevOps Personal Access Token
config.allowApproval: Offer the approving votes (*Approve*, and on Azure DevOps *Approve with suggestions*) when publishing a review. Off by default so a pull request is never approved from VS Code by mistake. Only user settings count: a repository cannot turn it on.
config.defaultEngine: Engine preselected by **Review with AI**: `copilot` (GitHub Copilot in VS Code) or a key of `#smartPrReview.engines#`.
config.engines: AI engines. An entry with `command` is a command-line engine: it gets the prompt on stdin, runs in a read-only worktree of the pull request and answers on stdout. The defaults keep Claude Code (restricted: no project hooks, settings or MCP servers), Codex (medium reasoning effort) and Cursor read-only and without web access; entries you add are merged with them. An engine with `modelArg` asks for the model on every review. An entry with `url` is a server with the OpenAI chat completions API (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenRouter…): it gets the changed files in the prompt and asks for the model on every review; set its API key, if it needs one, with **Set API Key of an AI Engine**. Machine-scoped: a repository cannot change it.
config.engines.modelArg: Flag of the command that selects the model, for example `--model`. With it, **Review with AI** asks for the model and appends the flag and the model to `args`.
config.engines.models: Models to offer when the review asks for one.
config.engines.listModelsArgs: Arguments that make the command print its models, one per line as `id` or `id - name`; they are added to the ones offered.
config.engines.defaultModel: Model offered first until you pick another one.
config.profilesPath: Folder of the repository with the review profiles (Markdown files with a `name` in their frontmatter).
config.aiLanguage: Language of the AI review comments and summary, for example `Spanish` or `English`. Empty: the language of the pull request title and description, or VS Code's display language when that is unclear.
config.aiTimeoutMinutes: Minutes an AI engine may take for one profile before it is stopped.
config.aiLabelComments: Add "Generated with AI · profile · engine" to the comments an AI review drafts, and "### profile (engine)" to its part of the summary.
welcome.noPullRequest:
No pull request is being reviewed. Pick one in **Pull Requests**, or search by number, title or author.
[Search Pull Requests](command:smartPrReview.searchPullRequests)
config.engines.url: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API, the part before `/chat/completions`, for example `http://localhost:11434/v1` (Ollama) or `http://localhost:1234/v1` (LM Studio). The pull request changes are sent there. Use it instead of `command`.
config.engines.contextWindow: Tokens the server takes per request, prompt and answer together: the context length the model was loaded with (`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` or `num_ctx` in Ollama, *Context Length* in LM Studio, `-c` in llama.cpp). A value above the server's lets it cut the prompt without notice. Only for engines with `url`.
config.engines.maxOutputTokens: Tokens of `contextWindow` kept for the answer, sent as `max_tokens`. Reasoning models spend them thinking too: give them room (for example 32768) or turn their reasoning down. Only for engines with `url`.
command.setEngineApiKey: Set API Key of an AI Engine
config.engines.reasoningEffort: How much a reasoning model thinks before answering: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `xhigh`, sent as `reasoning_effort`. Each model takes some of them (Qwen 3.8: `low`, `medium`, `xhigh`), and the server must support it (LM Studio 0.4.8 or later, vLLM, OpenRouter…); without it the model uses its default, often the highest. Less reasoning is faster and needs less `maxOutputTokens`. Only for engines with `url`.
